title: Grouped and Comparative Analysis
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of grouped and comparative analysis and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply group-wise summary statistics in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Grouped and Comparative Analysis is one step in Exploratory Data Analysis and Descriptive Statistics; exploratory data analysis generates questions and checks assumptions; descriptive summaries alone do not prove causality. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Use robust summaries and visual inspection, record exclusions, and keep the analysis reproducible. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.limitations: A descriptive statistic summarizes the sample; it does not replace checking its distribution. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For grouped and comparative analysis, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
